sections.h2: What should a seller know about Morgan County itself?
sections.html:
Morgan County is a west-central Illinois county of about 569 square miles of land, organized in 1823 from Greene and Sangamon counties and honoring the Cowpens victor Daniel Morgan. Jacksonville, laid out in 1825 on a tract near the county's center, serves as seat and biggest city, with Waverly the second city. Neighbors are Cass, Sangamon, Macoupin, Greene, Pike, Scott and Brown counties.

Interstate 72, US 36, US 67 and several state routes cross the county, and the 90th Meridian runs through it. Illinois College and the Illinois School for the Deaf and School for the Visually Impaired are in the county, and every school district that touches it is a full K-12 district. Jacksonville's January low averages 15 degrees and its July high 87, and May is the wettest month, so check basements and gutters before listing.

  • Population: 32,515 as of July 2025, against 35,547 in 2010.
  • Housing units: 14,987, with 72.8% owner-occupied.
  • Typical owned home: $130,800.
  • Median gross rent: $722.
  • Median household income: $66,306, with a 18.7 minute average commute.

Census QuickFacts supplies all of these numbers.

sections.h2: Which Morgan County offices handle the tax bill?
sections.html:
Billing and valuation live in different offices. The Treasurer, at 300 West State Street in Jacksonville, sends out bills and takes payment. The Supervisor of Assessments values every parcel and processes exemptions. Review of complaints falls to the three County Commissioners, with the Supervisor acting as clerk.

Illinois places two further players on your bill that the county cannot control: the township assessor, who does the first valuation, and the taxing districts, whose levies set the rate. The county's pages also list three tax increment financing districts, two in Jacksonville and one in Meredosia, and one enterprise zone in Jacksonville. Contact the city or village hall for details on those.

sections.h2: Which dates governed the 2025 Morgan County bills?
sections.html:
The bills for 2025, payable in 2026, ran on the calendar below. Every date has passed, and the pattern returns each year with new dates posted on the Treasurer's page.

Morgan County Treasurer schedule, tax year 2025 payable 2026
StepDate
Bills mailedMay 22, 2026
First installment dueJune 22, 2026
Mobile home tax dueJuly 22, 2026
Second installment dueSeptember 15, 2026
Certified funds onlyOctober 1, 2026
Judgment for sale of delinquent taxesOctober 28, 2026
Final day to pay at the counter before the saleOctober 30, 2026
Tax sale, Law Library of the courthouseNovember 2, 2026

Penalties on the first installment started June 23 at 1.5% and rose 1.5 points each month through October 23, when they reached 7.5%. The second installment began at 1.5% on September 16 and stepped to 3% on October 16. Mobile home penalties were $25 on July 23 and grew by $25 a month up to $100. A $10 certified mailing fee was added to accounts that received a certified letter. Friendly reminders went out September 25 and certified letters October 9, and would-be tax buyers had to register by October 16 with a $100 refundable fee.

sections.h2: How do you pay Morgan County property tax?
sections.html:
The Treasurer lists mail, a drop box, Morgan County banks other than US Bank, and an online portal. Mail goes to Morgan County Treasurer, 300 West State Street, Jacksonville, IL 62650, and the drop box sits outside the courthouse's north entrance, emptied each day by an employee.

  • Include the detachable stub from the bill with every payment.
  • Make checks payable to Morgan County Treasurer. A cancelled check is your receipt.
  • Returned checks carry a $25 charge, and post-dated checks are illegal and will not be held.
  • Only one bill comes each year, so keep the second stub. A duplicate bill costs $2.
  • Not getting a bill, or getting it late, never cancels the tax or penalty.

If the bill is not yours to pay, pass it to the owner or send it back to the Treasurer.

sections.h2: How does the Supervisor of Assessments value a Morgan County house?
sections.html:
Homes are valued at 33.33% of market value, with farmland and farm buildings treated separately. The office builds a house's value from square footage and story height, adds or subtracts for features such as bathrooms, central air, fireplaces, decks and garages, and then applies depreciation for age and condition. The base price assumes a full basement, central heat, one bath and a kitchen sink.

Land is valued as if vacant, by front foot, square foot, acreage or a flat site value for a whole area. Then the county and the state equalize values using three previous years of sales, which keeps one hot year from whipsawing assessments. Farm buildings are valued by use as well as size: the Supervisor's example is a newer pole building that sits idle, which can carry almost no contributory value. Mobile homes on piers are generally taxed through a privilege tax, while those on a permanent foundation are assessed as real estate and can claim the same exemptions as a frame or brick house.

sections.h2: What is the route for contesting a Morgan County value?
sections.html:
The clock is 30 days from publication of the assessment list, and the county says that notice usually runs in late December. The filing goes to the Supervisor by day 30 with a stated reason plus proof: a recent sale, comparables, an appraisal or neighboring assessments (35 ILCS 200/16-55).

Next, the Board mails a proposed change notice with the old value and any adjustment. Disagree, and you can call for a formal hearing. Once hearings end, final changes go out and the books close. An owner still unhappy can take the case to the state Property Tax Appeal Board, within 30 days of receiving the final notice, using forms kept at the assessor's office.

sections.h2: Which exemptions can a Morgan County homeowner claim?
sections.html:
Exemptions here go to people who own the home, live in it as a principal residence and are responsible for the tax; rentals and commercial or industrial property are excluded. For the general homestead exemption, a county not bordering one of 3 million people, as Morgan does not, has a $6,000 cap on the equalized value reduction (35 ILCS 200/15-175).

Ask the Supervisor's office which other exemptions fit your situation and when to file.

sections.h2: Who should a Morgan County seller call about taxes before closing day?
sections.html:
Begin at the Treasurer's counter and ask what each installment owes, plus any older delinquent year. State law counts a mailed payment as timely if postmarked by the due date, and sets first-installment delinquency at the later of June 1 or the day after the date on the bill (35 ILCS 200/21-15).

The title company splits the year between the parties at closing. If a lender escrows the tax, ask the servicer what it has already sent so nothing gets paid twice. Because the sale date in the Treasurer's calendar is the cutoff, an unpaid balance is best cleared before the October dates.

faqs.q: When did second installment penalties start on the 2025 bills?
faqs.a: They started September 16, 2026, at 1.5%, a day after the September 15 due date, and climbed to 3% on October 16. The first installment had been due June 22, 2026, with penalties starting the next day.

faqs.q: Can a Morgan County bill be paid at a bank?
faqs.a: Yes, at any Morgan County bank except US Bank. Mail, the drop box outside the courthouse's north entrance and the online portal also work.

faqs.q: What does a replacement bill cost?
faqs.a: The Treasurer charges $2.00 for a duplicate. One bill carries both installments each year, so keep it; a bill that never reached you does not remove the tax.

faqs.q: Who decides assessment complaints in Morgan County?
faqs.a: The three County Commissioners sit as the Board, with the Supervisor of Assessments as clerk. Appeals are accepted for 30 days following publication of the list.

faqs.q: Are there TIF districts in Morgan County?
faqs.a: Yes, three: two in Jacksonville and one in Meredosia, along with a single enterprise zone in Jacksonville. The local city or village hall has the rules for each.
